tasks.short: Write and edit broadcast scripts and video

steps.what: Verify the broadcast brief, source facts, footage rights and intended audience before choosing the story and clips
Write and edit scripts for broadcasts in {DOCS}, entering actual wording and checking names while native templates supply cue labels, timings and style flags
Edit video for the broadcast in the video-editing category of {OTHER}; select actual shots and sound while reusing native title and timecode presets
Watch the final video and read the final script for factual meaning, fair editing, pronunciation, rights, timing and technical quality; check the exact editorial handoff destination
Save the exact checked script and video versions in {DOCS}
Send the exact versioned broadcast package to the checked editor through {PROJECT}

tasks.design: Test native script cues and style rules in {DOCS} and title and timecode presets in the video-editing category of {OTHER}. Reuse formatting while the announcer writes actual copy, chooses footage and checks the final script and video together before saving and handing off the exact versions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated cue, title and timing setup interrupts editorial work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and presets can remove repeated formatting without generating factual claims.
tasks.still_hard: Fair selection, clear spoken wording and audiovisual meaning require editorial judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The announcer recognises when technically valid edits mislead the audience.
tasks.altitude: Less format setup, unchanged editorial accountability.

reach.task: Maintain meaningful continuity between shots and narration
reach.learn: Check that a cut does not distort what the speaker meant.

evidence.claim: Native document and video presets can reuse cues, titles and timings while editorial selection stays human.

assumptions: Boundary is announcer-authored scripts and video through editorial handoff, excluding the editor's approval and broadcast transmission. No outside-role saving is claimed.

The announcer verifies source claim, source reference, footage ID, rights status, cue wording and intended timecode in s1-s3. Existing station templates supply format and title fields. Missing rights or unclear sources require manual resolution; no unseen structured content producer is assumed.

Native configuration first. Illustrative shares assume repeated format setup, not a measured baseline; runtime is excluded. Final s4 checking occurs after both final artefacts exist and binds their versions and editorial recipient. Edits void both action approvals.
unknowns: How much formatting is already preset
Which final editorial checks are assigned to the announcer
research_questions: Which cue and title operations are repeated without changing editorial meaning?

already_counted.description: Actual authoring, video editing and final package review remain in s2-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain station presets and recheck changed export formats.

approvals.approved_version: Final script and video package checked in s4; any edit voids approval.
Same final package checked in s4 and saved unchanged in s5, to the editor destination checked in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Template and preset work saves 5 hours each in script and video editing: 10 gross less 2 upkeep gives 8 net. Existing presets give no gain. Facts, actual prose, shot judgement, final checks and handoff retain their effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Research the guest's life, work and current topic and prepare actual interview questions in {DOCS}; locate source items in the existing archive
Interview show guests about their lives, work or current topics; listen and ask follow-up questions without treating the prepared brief as their answers
Write and check actual interview follow-up notes and source pointers in {DOCS}
Save the exact checked interview notes in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Test native guest-name, topic and date filters in the {DOCS} archive to reduce source navigation. Reading, question writing, the actual interview and its ordinary notes stay with the announcer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant previous interviews can be scattered in the archive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing metadata filters can shorten navigation without inventing biography.
tasks.still_hard: Listening, trust and meaningful follow-up depend on the guest's actual replies.
tasks.human_edge: The announcer hears evasions and unexpected openings in a live conversation.

ambition.what: No new interview or publishing authority.

tasks.altitude: Slightly quicker preparation, unchanged guest relationship.

reach.learn: Trace background claims to their original sources.

evidence.claim: Archive filters can narrow source navigation but cannot replace reading or actual interviewing.

assumptions: Boundary is preparation, interview and actual follow-up notes, excluding separate recording release or broadcast transmission. No scheduled interview is treated as completed.

The booking record provides guest name, topic and date; existing source items provide author, date, title and source location. The announcer checks relevance and writes questions in s1. Missing metadata requires manual search; actual note capture remains counted in s3.

Native filters first; illustrative shares are not measured baselines. Only navigation changes, not biography reading or interview judgement. The ordinary s3 check covers the completed note version; edits void its save gate.
unknowns: How well guest metadata already works
Whether any archive navigation is repeated
research_questions: Can native filters reduce searching while preserving source reading?

already_counted.description: Source reading and question preparation remain in s1.

incremental.description: Correct archive metadata and maintain saved searches.

approvals.approved_version: Completed actual interview notes checked in s3; edits require rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Navigation removes 3 gross hours less 0.75 upkeep, or 2.25 net. Already searchable archives give zero benefit; conversation, capture and saving are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and deliver music, weather or traffic commentary

steps.what: Check current music metadata, weather or traffic source items, location and update time in the newsroom category of {OTHER}
Prepare and check the final short commentary in {DOCS}, including pronunciation, uncertainty, source freshness and the intended programme; reuse only native cue and timestamp fields
Comment on music, weather or traffic by delivering the checked final commentary to the intended programme audience

tasks.design: Use native cue and source-timestamp fields in {DOCS} for prepared commentary. Keep current-source checking, actual wording and delivery human; the announcer checks the completed wording and programme before speaking it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Short updates require repeated cue and source-time entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native fields can reuse that metadata without writing opinions or certifying current conditions.
tasks.still_hard: A fresh feed can still be incomplete or misleading.
tasks.human_edge: The announcer adjusts tone and gives uncertainty its proper weight.

ambition.what: No autonomous on-air voice or expanded editorial authority.

tasks.altitude: A small formatting reduction, unchanged public responsibility.

reach.task: Check source freshness before a bulletin
reach.learn: Separate a source timestamp from the time conditions actually occurred.

evidence.claim: Cue and timestamp fields can be reused deterministically while commentary meaning remains human-authored.

assumptions: Boundary is a prepared short commentary item, not spontaneous unscripted discussion. This delivery action is the announcer's speaking time, not transmission-system runtime. No separate script-save or producer approval baseline is invented.

The source provider supplies item ID, source text, place and update time; programme metadata supplies destination. The announcer verifies these in s1 and writes and checks final words in s2. Missing or stale source data require manual checking or omission, not fabricated facts.

Native fields first; illustrative shares are not measured baselines. The ordinary final s2 check follows completion of the wording and binds the exact programme and facts; changed wording or conditions require rechecking before delivery.
unknowns: Whether cue fields are already automatic
How much commentary is prepared rather than improvised
research_questions: Is repeated metadata entry material in actual prepared updates?

already_counted.description: Actual wording and final editorial checking remain in s2.

incremental.description: Maintain source-field mappings and detect timestamp changes.

approvals.approved_version: Final commentary and programme checked after wording is complete in s2; any factual, wording or destination change requires rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Metadata entry saves 2.5 gross hours less 0.5 upkeep for 2 net in a manual-cue scenario. Native cues already set up give no gain. Source verification and actual speaking are retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Represent the employer at promotional appearances

steps.what: Read the event brief, agreed employer messages and event format before making the promotional appearance
Make the promotional appearance at the public or private event, representing the employer through presence and interactions with attendees

tasks.design: Keep brief reading and the actual promotional appearance human. No record write, report, media send or booking transaction is specified in this appearance task, so none is invented to manufacture an administrative saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: The employer is represented through a real person's presence and responses.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated mechanism changes that appearance work.
tasks.still_hard: Audience rapport and unexpected questions are situational.
tasks.human_edge: The announcer represents the employer personally and responds in context.

reach.learn: Understand which claims the employer has actually approved.

evidence.claim: Physical appearances depend on presence and audience interaction.

assumptions: Boundary is preparing for and making the appearance, excluding separately assigned booking, travel administration, promotional-content publication and follow-up reports. The task statement requires no record or send; such work needs a confirmed baseline before inclusion.

The event organiser and employer supply the existing brief, event time, venue, format and agreed messages. The announcer reads and clarifies them in s1. Missing information is clarified manually; no new capture system is proposed.
Illustrative shares are not measured. Native document access already supports the brief; no new tool, configuration or upkeep is proposed.
unknowns: Whether actual appearance assignments include separately required reports
research_questions: Is any required administrative output part of this task in the organisation?

already_counted.description: Brief reading and actual appearance remain in s1-s2.

incremental.description: No new tool or procedure, so zero additional upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No change to brief reading or physical appearance is established after checking for actual record and send outputs. No unobserved administration baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Format setup can shrink while editorial judgement, interviews and personal appearances remain human.
reach: Understand producer research and video-editor continuity checks.
role.ambitious_version: An announcer who spends less time setting up formats and more time understanding guests and the audience.

job.title: Broadcast Announcers and Radio Disc Jockeys
